overview: Valdemar of Sweden was Swedish king and son of Birger Jarl whose reign ended with deposition by his brother Magnus. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1250 — Becomes king; 1266 — Rules after Birger’s death; 1275 — Deposed.
He died in 1302, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Overview

He died in 1302, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Valdemar of Sweden was born c. 1239. His family background is usually placed in House of Bjälbo, though early Scandinavian genealogy can be uncertain and politically shaped.

Valdemar of Sweden's early life belonged to the medieval Scandinavian world, where kinship, sea routes, church contacts, assemblies, and armed followings shaped the opportunities available to a ruler.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Valdemar of Sweden, first of the Folkung dynasty to wear the crown, is remembered as a king overshadowed by his powerful father Birger Jarl and then destroyed by rivalry with his own brothers. The sources present a ruler who came to the throne as a boy under his father's guidance and who, after Birger's death, proved unable to hold his own against his ambitious siblings, losing power and eventually his freedom.

A scandal involving his sister-in-law and a penitential journey damaged his reputation, and the tradition tends to present him as weak, pleasure-loving, and politically ineffective compared with the brothers who supplanted him. Such moralising should be treated with caution, as it served the interests of those who deposed him.

What survives is largely the image of a king who could not master his family or his nobles, defined more by his fall than by any positive achievement. He is remembered as the ineffective first Folkung monarch, his individual qualities obscured by the partisan memory of his more successful rivals.

contentSections.title: As king of Sweden
paragraphs: Valdemar became king as a child, with Birger Jarl as the real power behind the throne. After Birger’s death, conflict with his brothers weakened him.
As King of Sweden, Valdemar of Sweden had to turn dynastic claim into workable authority through alliances, military pressure, church support, and acceptance by regional elites.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Died in 1302 after deposition and confinement, a victim of the dynastic struggle that brought his brother Magnus III to power.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: His reign marks the beginning of Bjälbo kingship, but his political legacy was overshadowed by Magnus Ladulås.
Later saga, saintly, or national traditions often amplified Valdemar of Sweden's reputation, so the article separates near-contemporary evidence from later memory where possible.

timeline.title: Born
timeline.description: Valdemar of Sweden was born around c. 1239, but the birthplace is not securely recorded. The date is approximate, but it places the early life in the setting of Kingdom of Sweden.

timeline.title: Birth chronology
timeline.description: Valdemar of Sweden's birth chronology is approximate; the 1239 label reflects the range used for this article rather than a precisely documented birthday.

timeline.title: Becomes king
timeline.description: Valdemar became king as a child after the extinction of the Erik line, while his father Birger Jarl held real political power.

timeline.title: Rules after Birger’s death
timeline.description: After Birger Jarl died in 1266, Valdemar had to rule without his father’s authority and soon faced pressure from his brothers.

timeline.title: Deposed
timeline.description: Valdemar was defeated and deposed by his brother Magnus after the Battle of Hova, ending his effective kingship.
